question: All urinary tract infections caused by ESBL-producing E. coli require intravenous carbapenem therapy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. While carbapenems are indicated for complicated or systemic ESBL infections (e.g. pyelonephritis, urosepsis), uncomplicated lower UTIs can be effectively treated with oral fosfomycin or nitrofurantoin when the isolate is susceptible. Reflexive carbapenem use drives unnecessary resistance selection.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Uncomplicated lower UTIs caused by ESBL-producing E. coli can be treated with oral fosfomycin or nitrofurantoin (when susceptible), per IDSA and ICMR guidance. Reserving carbapenems for complicated or systemic ESBL infections is a core antimicrobial stewardship principle.
